source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
page_notation: printed book pages, not PDF leaf indices
policy: Append source-specific research only, preserve originals and photo credits; BONAP deferred.

morphology.habit: Taprooted annual or biennial, stems 30–100 cm, mostly unbranched near base and glabrous per key
morphology.leaves: Basal rosette often deciduous; 3–9 stem leaves, uppermost entire/toothed or with one pair of lobes
morphology.heads: Large all-yellow ligulate heads; outer phyllaries 1/3–2/3 length of inner, principal phyllaries 15–25 mm
morphology.fruit: Beaked cypselae 14–17 mm including beak; genus capillary pappus 7–12 mm

qa_notes: Can hybridize with P. pauciflorus where soils are mixed along roadsides; do not identify solely from flower color.

morphology.habit: Perennial with tuber 5–20 mm thick, located 2–15 cm underground, producing shallow rhizomes; stems 10–30(–40) cm
morphology.stems: Usually curly-pubescent, 0–2 stem leaves or bracts
morphology.heads: Yellow, entirely ligulate, principal phyllaries 15–20 mm
morphology.fruit: Beaked cypselae 10–13 mm and capillary pappus (genus)

qa_notes: Tuberous rootstock distinguishes from taprooted annual congeners; do not infer a tuber from an aboveground photograph.

morphology.habit: Taprooted annual 20–60 cm, stems mostly branching from base, with curly hairs
morphology.leaves: Basal rosette, 1–5 stem leaves, uppermost deeply several-lobed
morphology.heads: Yellow entirely ligulate heads, principal phyllaries 16–20 mm, outer phyllaries usually ≤1/3 inner length
morphology.fruit: Beaked cypselae 12–14 mm; capillary pappus 7–12 mm (genus)

qa_notes: Regional flora reports occasional hybridization with P. carolinianus in disturbed mixed soil settings.

morphology.habit: Perennial often flowering first year, stems 0.2–1.2 m, finely scabrous pubescent
morphology.leaves: Alternate, compound/deeply lobed with narrow linear or lanceolate terminal segments
morphology.heads: Long peduncles; elongated column-like receptacle 1.5–4.5 cm
morphology.rays: 3–7 functionally infertile, 10–20(–35) mm, yellow or yellow-orange, bases sometimes reddish-brown, spreading/reflexed
morphology.disk: Perfect fertile yellow-brown flowers; receptacular scales gray pubescent
morphology.fruit: Pappus one minute awn ca. 0.6 mm, sometimes second shorter awn
morphology.habitat: Sandy, silty or rocky open sites

qa_notes: Flower color varies within species; elongated receptacle is more reliable.

morphology.leaves: Alternate, oblong to ovate with distinctly heart-shaped clasping bases, margins entire or toothed
morphology.heads: Peduncled, short cylindrical composite heads; elongated chaffy receptacle with green-tipped paleae
morphology.rays: 5–10 infertile, 10–25 mm yellow ligules, sometimes brown-purple blotched at base
morphology.disks: Perfect fertile florets with brownish/purple tubular corollas
morphology.fruit: Cylindric to club-shaped cypselae, pappus absent

qa_notes: Historic transfer to Dracopis is explicit, not an arbitrary name match.
Species usually treated with Rudbeckia now; modern accepted-name validation separate.

records.printed_page: Rudbeckia hirta L. var. pulcherrima Farw.

morphology.habit: Coarsely hairy annual to short-lived perennial (regional variety description)
morphology.leaves: Alternate, basal and cauline blades narrowed to bases, subsessile/sessile, rough hairy
morphology.heads: Large yellow-orange radiate heads, sometimes reddish/purple at ray base
morphology.receptacle: Disk receptacular paleae bear apical bristles; style branches elongate and awl-like per key

qa_notes: Regional flora gives variety pulcherrima, not blanket species-level morphology for all varieties; keep variety provenance.

morphology.habit: Robust 1–3 m glaucous perennial, sometimes in beds/colonies
morphology.leaves: Blue-green glabrous broad ovate to oblong blades, upper ones sessile and partly clasping
morphology.heads: Large terminal yellow-rayed heads; dark disks elongate strikingly in fruit to 4–8 cm
morphology.rays: Yellow to orange-yellow 3–8 cm × ≤12 mm, infertile
morphology.disk: Perfect fertile florets, chaff tips pubescent

qa_notes: Long ripening disk and glaucous leaves distinguish from R. hirta.

morphology.habit: Loosely woolly to nearly glabrous annual 30–80 cm
morphology.leaves: Alternate, low leaves narrowing to small petiolar base but clasping at node; upper leaves truncate-clasping; mostly entire/shallowly toothed
morphology.heads: Cymose terminal yellow radiate heads, involucres 7–11 mm; main and accessory phyllaries green-tipped
morphology.fruit: Cylindrical cypselae, white capillary pappus per genus
morphology.habitat: Sandy open woods, fields and roadsides

qa_notes: Genus key contrasts black-tipped phyllaries and inconspicuous rays of introduced S. vulgaris; do not confuse.

morphology.leaves: Alternate, deeply pinnatifid, rigid and very scabrous; blades nearly as wide as long, often vertically oriented
morphology.heads: Large heads in raceme-like grouping, WHITE rays 25 mm per key
morphology.reproductive: Fertile ray florets produce flattened winged fruits; central disk florets staminate/infertile (genus)
morphology.fruit: Cypselae puberulent, wings extending beyond body into V-notch ~3–5 mm deep

qa_notes: Compare S. laciniatum yellow rays, taller habit, less-deep fruit-wing notch.

morphology.habit: Coarse perennial 1–3 m from woody crown/taproot
morphology.leaves: Alternate very stiff, vertically held, deeply pinnatifid, usually longer than wide
morphology.heads: Raceme-like yellow-rayed heads, rays 25–40 mm in flora key
morphology.reproductive: Ray florets fertile, disk florets functionally staminate and do not set seed
morphology.fruit: Glabrous or nearly glabrous winged cypselae, V-shaped apical notch 1–3 mm deep

qa_notes: Leaf orientation is variable and not enough by itself for identification.

morphology.leaves: Usually broad sessile entire or slightly toothed, alternating or opposite within populations; well-developed upper leaves near heads
morphology.heads: Solitary/few in corymb-like array with relatively short peduncles; yellow rays
morphology.reproductive: Fertile ray florets yield winged cypselae; disk florets functionally staminate
morphology.pubescence: Coarse stem hairs can be ~1 mm or longer, but regional flora notes substantial overlap with related taxa

qa_notes: Flora documents ambiguity with S. integrifolium and intergradation with S. gracile; do not key by hairs or alternate/opposite alone.

morphology.habit: Introduced Mediterranean coarse annual/biennial (rarely perennial) 0.6–1.8+ m
morphology.leaves: Alternate striking white-mottled green, spiny-lobed; cauline leaves ear-clasping but NOT decurrent down the stem
morphology.heads: Large terminal 2.5–6 cm heads; involucre bracts to 5 cm with very broad base and spiny tapering tips
morphology.fruit: White non-plumose pappus bristles 15–20 mm, shed together as ring

qa_notes: Regionally introduced; avoid nativity inference from Texas occurrence.

holds.name: Rudbeckia amplexicaulis
holds.issue: Flora treatment under Dracopis; transfer checked within source but independent modern nomenclatural reconciliation outstanding.

holds.name: Rudbeckia hirta
holds.issue: Flora species treatment is at var. pulcherrima, not full species concept.
